html:
Agent Orange was a herbicide sprayed by the US military over South Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia from 1962 to 1971, in Operation Ranch Hand, to strip the jungle cover and destroy crops.

Planes sprayed tens of millions of litres of herbicides, Agent Orange the most used, over forests, mangroves and fields. It was tainted with dioxin, one of the most toxic substances known, which lingers in soil and food. The Vietnamese government says millions were exposed and that hundreds of thousands of children were born with defects; American veterans also fell ill.

The United States long denied responsibility for Vietnamese victims but paid veterans from 1991. Since 2012 it has paid to clean up dioxin hot spots at former air bases, such as Da Nang. Agent Orange remains one of the bitterest legacies of the American war and of the Vietnam War as a whole, and a reason the destruction of nature in war, ecocide, is now argued over in law.
sum: Agent Orange was a herbicide sprayed by the US military over South Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia from 1962 to 1971, in Operation Ranch Hand, to strip the jungle cover and destroy crops.
